db-first-steps.title: Define your first model
db-first-steps.goal: Describe a **Book** to the database: a required `title`, an `author` that defaults to `'Unknown'`, and a numeric `year`.
hints: Each field is a key inside the object you pass to `new mongoose.Schema({ ... })`.
A field can be just a type (`year: Number`) or an options object: `{ type: String, required: true }`.
Defaults go in the options object too: `author: { type: String, default: 'Unknown' }`.

db-first-steps.title: Save and read books
db-first-steps.goal: Write `addBook`, `listBooks` (oldest first) and `findByAuthor`. The model is ready in `models/Book.js`.
hints: `Model.create(data)` saves a document and resolves to it. Return it.
`Model.find()` with no filter returns everything. Chain `.sort({ year: 1 })` for ascending.
A filter is a plain object: `Book.find({ author: name })`.

db-queries.title: Filter by price
db-queries.goal: Use comparison operators: `cheaperThan(max)` (strictly below, cheapest first) and `inPriceRange(min, max)` (both ends included).
hints: Operators go inside the field's value: `{ price: { $lt: 10 } }`.
`$lt` is strictly less than; `$lte`, `$gte` include the boundary.
Combine two operators on one field: `{ price: { $gte: min, $lte: max } }`.

db-queries.title: Tags and search
db-queries.goal: `withAnyTag(tags)` returns products having at least one of the tags. `searchByName(q)` matches names containing `q`, ignoring case.
hints: When a field holds an array, `{ tags: 'x' }` already means "contains x". For several options use `$in`.
Case-insensitive contains: `{ name: { $regex: q, $options: 'i' } }`.
User text inside a regex must be escaped, or `.` matches everything: `q.replace(/[.*+?^$()|[\]\\{}]/g, '\\$&')`.

db-express-api.title: Your first database-backed API
db-express-api.goal: Finish the controller: `POST /todos` saves a todo (201, or 400 when `title` is missing), `GET /todos/:id` returns it (404 if missing, 400 for a malformed id).
hints: Read the body from `req.body.title`. If it's missing, `return res.status(400).json({ error: '...' })`. The `return` stops the handler.
`Todo.create(...)` saves; reply with `res.status(201).json(todo)`.
Check the id first with `mongoose.isValidObjectId(id)` (400), then `findById` returns `null` when nothing matches (404).

db-updates.title: Update without losing stock
db-updates.goal: `restock` should return the **updated** product. `buy` must never sell more than is in stock, even when two orders arrive at once.
hints: `findByIdAndUpdate` returns the document as it was **before** the update unless you pass `{ new: true }`.
In `buy`, the read and the write are separate steps. Two requests can both read `stock: 1` before either saves.
Make it one atomic step: `Product.updateOne({ _id: id, stock: { $gte: qty } }, { $inc: { stock: -qty } })`, then check `modifiedCount === 1`.

db-relations.title: Posts and their authors
db-relations.goal: Posts reference users. `postsWithAuthors()` returns every post with its `author` filled in (sorted by title), and `postsBy(userId)` returns one user's posts.

support.models/User.js:
import mongoose from 'mongoose';

export default mongoose.model('User', new mongoose.Schema({ name: { type: String, required: true } }));

hints: The post only stores the author's `_id`. `.populate('author')` swaps it for the user document.
`populate` chains like `sort`: `Post.find().sort(...).populate('author')`.
To filter by a reference, compare the id field: `Post.find({ author: userId })`.

db-pagination.title: Pages that add up
db-pagination.goal: `listPage(page, limit)` returns `{ items, page, total, totalPages }`. Pages start at 1, items are sorted by `n`, and `limit` is capped at 50.

support.models/Item.js:
import mongoose from 'mongoose';

export default mongoose.model('Item', new mongoose.Schema({ n: Number }));

hints: Page 1 should skip nothing: `skip((page - 1) * limit)`.
Without `.sort({ n: 1 })` the order is whatever the database feels like, so pages can repeat or skip items.
`total` is the size of the whole collection: `Item.countDocuments()`, not `items.length`. Then `totalPages = Math.ceil(total / limit)`.

db-aggregate.title: Your first report
db-aggregate.goal: Group orders: `totalsByCategory()` returns `{ _id: category, total, count }` sorted by total, highest first. `topCustomers(n)` returns the n biggest spenders as `{ _id: customer, spent }`.
hints: `aggregate` takes an array of stages. Each document flows through them in order.
`{ $group: { _id: '$category', total: { $sum: '$amount' } } }`: the `$` in `'$amount'` means "the value of this field". `{ $sum: 1 }` counts.
Add `{ $sort: { total: -1 } }` after the group, and `{ $limit: n }` for the top-n.

db-errors.title: Turn database errors into status codes
db-errors.goal: `POST /users` creates a user (201). A validation failure is **400**, a duplicate email is **409**, and the password never comes back in the response.
hints: Look at the error before answering: `err.name === 'ValidationError'` means the input broke a schema rule, so it's the client's fault (400).
A unique index violation has `err.code === 11000`. That's a conflict: 409.
Respond with only safe fields, e.g. `{ id: user._id, email: user.email }`, instead of the whole document.
